docs.abstract: Flight was probably more widespread in dinosaurs than previously thought. A newly identified species sheds light on how some achieved liftoff.

headline.main: What Can Four-Winged Dinosaurs Teach Us About Birds?

multimedia.caption: The fossil, discovered by a local farmer, revealed several aerial adaptations like fused bones in the wrist, elongated bones in the forearm that would have made for a more powerful wing and an enlarged breastbone to anchor flight muscles.
multimedia.credit: Andrea Cau et al. and the Museum of Hebei GEO University, Shijiazhuang, China
